names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Απριλίου, «Άγιοι Θεοδώρα και Δίδυμος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 27. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученици Теодора и Дидим“ — Свети is not a rank, мученици is the `martyr` this corpus puts in `types`, and Дидим is her companion and not part of her name. The body gives „Теодора девица“, and **девица is the `virgin` already in `types`, so it is stripped too** and the bare personal name is what is stored. **Measured, and it is a wide fold entered on purpose**: `foldchk.py` returns four folders already holding a bare «Теодора» — `theodora-12-january`, `theodora-companion-of-leonides`, `theodora-of-alexandria` and `theodora-the-empress` — so this makes a fifth, and the corpus keeps ten more Theodoras that hold no `sr` form at all. **There is no fuller form to prefer**: the heading prints the two names and nothing else, and Alexandria is the other books’ and not this heading’s to attach. The Greek form on this folder, «Θεοδώρα», is the same bare name.

The heading of the calendar’s name link, «Феодора Александрийская, дева, мц.», with the two rank words after the comma left off. The city is the calendar’s own and the life bears it out. The day’s own line gives «Феодоры девы». THIS FORM WIDENED A FOLD AND THE CLAIM FIRST WRITTEN HERE WAS WRONG: the note said `fk.mjs` had returned NONE for «александрииская феодора», and `fk.mjs` had not been run on this form at all. It returns `theodora-of-alexandria`, which already stores the identical Russian string. The plain gate printed the new collision as unread, the key ‘александрииская феодора theodora-companion-of-didymus theodora-of-alexandria’ was written in the same commit, and its membership is exactly those two folders. The bare «Феодора» was deliberately not stored, this corpus holding a great many of that name.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 27 мая ст. ст. — «Мчч. Феодоры девы и Дидима воина (304).»

attestations.note: The identification is exact: the line pairs the virgin and the soldier as this folder’s display name does, and its Greek and Serbian rows keep the same pair on the same Julian day. The calendar gives the two of them one page, life1149. `dates` is unchanged: the folder holds 304 off the Охридски пролог and the day line prints the same year, while the life says «в 303 или 304 году» — a choice of two the folder’s single year is one of, and it was not widened to the pair. `virgin` already stands and the line’s «девы» bears it out. What the Russian adds and the paragraph carries: the city of Alexandria and the governor Евстратий, her answer that she had given herself to God and chosen to stay a virgin for the Name of Christ, the three days given her in prison to think and the threat of the brothel, the brothel and the young men quarrelling over who should go in first, Didymus coming in unhindered in his soldier’s dress and driving them out and giving her his clothes, his trial and sentence, her coming to the place of his execution to say she wished to die with him, her bowing her head under the sword first, and the burning of the bodies. azbyka.ru was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 5ης Απριλίου — «Άγιοι Θεοδώρα και Δίδυμος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 5 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. It puts the martyrdom «κατά τον πιο άγριο διωγμό της Εκκλησίας, επί Διοκλητιανού» and gives no year at all, so there are no dates here. She is not the venerable Theodora of Alexandria whom the same calendar keeps on 11 September.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 09.06.2026 (27. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Теодора и Дидим“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, whose heading names her first. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23 to 27 May is — note that the 7 May and 24 April headings quoted elsewhere in this wave do carry one, so this is the page and not a transcription habit. **A DAY NEITHER OTHER CALENDAR KEEPS THE PAIR ON.** saint.gr keeps them together on 5 April and the Romanian and Russian rows are `undocumented`, so the row is written on the 27/5 and the Greek row is left on the 5/4. The day list for the menologion 27/5 could not see either of them for that reason, and **`sr-namesweep.mjs` found them because the heading prints both names** — the one shape of enumerated company it does manage, two names with the first one scored. **FIRST DATES FOR BOTH, AND THE EMPEROR DISAGREES.** Neither folder has had a `dates` object: the existing life records „The page gives no year, names no relics and prints no hymn under either of them.“ The Prologue states one — „Чесно пострадаше и задобише венце вечне славе 304. године у Александрији“ — so `dates.death` is 304 to 304, `basis: "traditional"`, with the book’s own words in the note. **The reign is used for nothing, and it is the reign the two books differ on**: this entry opens „У време злочестивог цара Максимилијана“, Maximian, where saint.gr puts the martyrdom „in the fiercest persecution the Church knew, under Diocletian“. **No year was derived from either reign and neither emperor was chosen**; both stand in the prose. **AND THE PROLOGUE NAMES NO EPARCH WHERE SAINT.GR NAMES EUSTRATIUS**, calling him only „кнез мучитељ“ and „судија“. Nothing was reconciled: a persecutor gains no folder by the coordinator’s third ruling and the existing life keeps the Greek page’s name for him. **THE EXECUTION IS A DIFFERENT SCENE IN EACH BOOK, AND THIS ONE IS THE DIALOGUE.** saint.gr has Didymus beheaded and burnt, and then Theodora present herself to the eparch, reproach him for the killing and be thrown into the flames. **The Prologue has her run to the place of execution and argue with Didymus himself**: „Иако си ти спасао моју част, ја нисам од тебе искала да ме спасеш од смрти. Уступи мени смрт мученичку!“ — though you saved my honour, I did not ask you to save me from death; yield me the martyr’s death — and his answer, „Возљубљена сестро, не спречавај ме да умрем за Христа и крвљу мојом оперем грехе моје!“ **And the pagans, hearing the quarrel, condemned them both**, and **both were beheaded and both bodies burnt**, where saint.gr has her burnt alive. **Both tellings are written and neither is resolved.** **«сестро» IS NOT A KINSHIP.** He calls her beloved sister at the scaffold and nothing in either book makes them kin; the two folders were already `related` to each other in both directions as companions, and no row was added or changed. No `locations`, although Alexandria is named in both books. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. **Of her in particular, new**: that she was **of noble birth and upbringing** — „благородног происхођења и васпитања“ — which saint.gr does not say; that she was brought to trial **as a Christian** and examined long for the faith of Christ before the sentence; and that **while she was praying earnestly that God save her from defilement, the soldier came in** — the Prologue makes her prayer the cause of his coming where saint.gr makes it Didymus’s own resolve on hearing of her danger. **It also says that it was she who was let out and he who stayed behind in the brothel**, which saint.gr leaves unsaid. `martyr` and `virgin` are both corroborated — „Теодора девица“ — and **no type was added**; `virgin` was already stored, so the `virgin-martyr` that `honorific.js` composes from `martyr` plus `virgin` is what this folder already prints and nothing about it changed, which is the opposite case to the `virgin` refused on `john-vladimir` on 22 May.

death.note: Охридски пролог за 09.06.2026 (27. мај ст. ст.): „Чесно пострадаше и задобише венце вечне славе 304. године у Александрији“. The first year any calendar read for this folder states; saint.gr gives none. The entry opens „У време злочестивог цара Максимилијана“ where saint.gr puts the martyrdom under Diocletian; both reigns are recorded in the life and no year was derived from either.
